schema_description: openEHR Access Log: a draft change proposal for a record of every access to EHR data, kept outside the EHR as an append-only, hash-chained log keyed by ehr_id. Not an openEHR release.

ACCESS_LOG_RECORD.name: ACCESS_LOG_RECORD
ACCESS_LOG_RECORD.documentation: Abstract parent of the records of an access log. Each record holds one link of the log's hash chain, so the order and the completeness of the log can be verified by anyone who reads it. A record is never modified; when its retention period ends, the system replaces an `ACCESS_LOG_ENTRY` by an `ACCESS_LOG_TOMBSTONE` that keeps the uid, the time and the link.

uid.name: uid
uid.documentation: Unique identifier of this record, assigned by the recording system.

system_id.name: system_id
system_id.documentation: Identifier of the logical EHR system that recorded the access, with the meaning of `AUDIT_DETAILS._system_id_`.

time_recorded.name: time_recorded
time_recorded.documentation: Time at which the record was written to the log.

link.name: link
link.documentation: This record's link in the log's hash chain.

ACCESS_LOG_ENTRY.name: ACCESS_LOG_ENTRY
ACCESS_LOG_ENTRY.documentation: The record of one access event to the data of at most one EHR: who accessed, on whose behalf, what, when, why, under which authorisation, with which outcome, and through which channel. An access that reaches the data of several EHRs is recorded as one entry per EHR, and the entries of one request share `_channel.request_id_`.

occurred.name: occurred
occurred.documentation: Time interval over which the access took place, when it is known and differs from `_time_recorded_`.

action.name: action
action.documentation: What the access did to the data, coded in the openEHR Terminology `access action` group.

operation.name: operation
operation.documentation: The interface operation that carried the access, such as an ITS-REST operation id, coded in a terminology that names the interface.

outcome.name: outcome
outcome.documentation: Whether the access was granted, and how it ended.

accessor.name: accessor
accessor.documentation: Who accessed the data, on whose behalf, and with which credential.

ehr_id.name: ehr_id
ehr_id.documentation: The `ehr_id` of the EHR whose data the access reached or asked for. Void only for an access that named no EHR, such as a refused request whose target could not be resolved.

items.name: items
items.documentation: The data of the EHR the access asked for or delivered.

query.name: query
query.documentation: The query that carried the access, for an access by query.

purposes.name: purposes
purposes.documentation: The purposes of use the accessor declared or the system established.

authorisations.name: authorisations
authorisations.documentation: The grounds on which the access was authorised or refused: roles, agreements, consent decisions, permits, emergency overrides.

is_emergency.name: is_emergency
is_emergency.documentation: True when the access was made under an emergency override of the access policy, such as an access to protect the vital interests of the subject of care.

channel.name: channel
channel.documentation: The interface and the request that carried the access.

security_labels.name: security_labels
security_labels.documentation: Labels that limit who may read this entry, derived from the categories and origins of the data accessed.

retention.name: retention
retention.documentation: How long this entry is kept, and on which grounds.

other_details.name: other_details
other_details.documentation: Further details a jurisdiction or a deployment records, never clinical content. May be archetyped.

ACCESS_LOG_TOMBSTONE.name: ACCESS_LOG_TOMBSTONE
ACCESS_LOG_TOMBSTONE.documentation: What remains of an `ACCESS_LOG_ENTRY` after its retention period: the uid, the recording time and the chain link, so the chain still verifies, and nothing that identifies a person or the data.

time_removed.name: time_removed
time_removed.documentation: Time at which the entry's content was removed.

grounds.name: grounds
grounds.documentation: The grounds of the removal: the end of the retention period, or an erasure a law orders.

ACCESS_LOG_LINK.name: ACCESS_LOG_LINK
ACCESS_LOG_LINK.documentation: One link of the hash chain of an access log. `_content_digest_` is the digest of the record's canonical serialisation without its link; `_digest_` is the digest over `_previous_digest_`, `_sequence_` and `_content_digest_`, so a removed or reordered record breaks every later link while a tombstone, which keeps the content digest, does not.

sequence.name: sequence
sequence.documentation: Position of the record in the log of its `_system_id_`, starting at 1, with no gaps.

algorithm.name: algorithm
algorithm.documentation: Name of the digest algorithm, such as `SHA-256`.

previous_digest.name: previous_digest
previous_digest.documentation: The `_digest_` of the preceding record, in lower-case hexadecimal; for the first record, the digest the log was started with.

content_digest.name: content_digest
content_digest.documentation: Digest of the record's canonical serialisation with `_link_` removed, in lower-case hexadecimal.

digest.name: digest
digest.documentation: Digest over `_previous_digest_`, `_sequence_` and `_content_digest_`, in lower-case hexadecimal.

signature.name: signature
signature.documentation: Optional signature of the recording system over `_digest_`, for a jurisdiction that asks for each record to be signed.

invariants.Digests_valid: not previous_digest.is_empty and not content_digest.is_empty and not digest.is_empty

ACCESS_LOG_CHECKPOINT.name: ACCESS_LOG_CHECKPOINT
ACCESS_LOG_CHECKPOINT.documentation: A signed statement by the recording system of the head of its log at a point in time. A checkpoint commits to every record up to `_sequence_`, so a verifier that holds it can detect a later rewrite of the log, and an export carries the checkpoint its records verify against.

system_id.name: system_id
system_id.documentation: The system whose log the checkpoint seals.

sequence.name: sequence
sequence.documentation: The `_link.sequence_` of the last record the checkpoint covers.

algorithm.name: algorithm
algorithm.documentation: Name of the digest algorithm of the chain.

time_sealed.name: time_sealed
time_sealed.documentation: Time at which the checkpoint was signed.

signer.name: signer
signer.documentation: The party, usually the organisation responsible for the system, whose key signed the checkpoint.

proof.name: proof
proof.documentation: The signature over the checkpoint's other attributes, in the form `ATTESTATION._proof_` uses, such as a JWS or a PGP signature.

ACCESSOR.name: ACCESSOR
ACCESSOR.documentation: Who accessed: the party, the healthcare provider they acted for, their roles and groups, the credential they presented, and the chain of clients and parties that acted between them and the system.

kind.name: kind
kind.documentation: The kind of accessor, coded in the openEHR Terminology `accessor kind` group: a person, a person through a delegated client, the subject of care, a representative, a person of another organisation, an organisation, or a system acting for nobody.

party.name: party
party.documentation: The party that accessed: `PARTY_IDENTIFIED` with an `_external_ref_` to the demographic party the system bound the caller to, `PARTY_SELF` for the subject of care, `PARTY_RELATED` for a representative, or `PARTY_IDENTIFIED` with identifiers alone where no party is known here.

provider.name: provider
provider.documentation: The healthcare provider or other organisation the accessor acted for.

roles.name: roles
roles.documentation: The functional or security roles the accessor held for the access.

groups.name: groups
groups.documentation: The demographic `GROUP` parties, such as care teams, whose membership the access relied on.

binding.name: binding
binding.documentation: How the system bound the credential to `_party_`, or why it could not, coded in a terminology the system names.

credential.name: credential
credential.documentation: The credential the accessor authenticated with.

delegation.name: delegation
delegation.documentation: The clients and parties that acted between the accessor and the system, outermost first, as the credential named them.

ACCESS_CREDENTIAL.name: ACCESS_CREDENTIAL
ACCESS_CREDENTIAL.documentation: A reference to a credential, by its issuer and the identifiers it carried, never the credential itself.

issuer.name: issuer
issuer.documentation: The issuer of the credential, such as an OAuth 2.0 authorization server's issuer identifier or a SAML IdP's entity id.

client_id.name: client_id
client_id.documentation: The client the credential was issued to.

token_id.name: token_id
token_id.documentation: The identifier of the token or assertion, such as a JWT `jti`.

assurance.name: assurance
assurance.documentation: The assurance level of the authentication.

authentication_method.name: authentication_method
authentication_method.documentation: The authentication method or context class the issuer stated.

result.name: result
result.documentation: The result, coded in the openEHR Terminology `access outcome` group: granted, partially granted, refused or failed.

reason.name: reason
reason.documentation: Why the access was refused, partly granted or failed, coded in the openEHR Terminology `access refusal reason` group or a terminology the system names.

description.name: description
description.documentation: Free text on the outcome, never clinical content.

delivered.name: delivered
delivered.documentation: The number of objects or result rows delivered to the accessor, when counted.

ACCESSED_ITEM.name: ACCESSED_ITEM
ACCESSED_ITEM.documentation: One item of EHR data an access asked for or delivered: a versioned object or one of its versions, or, for a query whose result is not itemised, the categories and origins of what it delivered.

object.name: object
object.documentation: Reference to the versioned object, `EHR_STATUS`, `EHR_ACCESS` or directory the item belongs to.

version_id.name: version_id
version_id.documentation: The version accessed, when one version was.

rm_type.name: rm_type
rm_type.documentation: The reference model type of the item, such as `COMPOSITION`.

archetype_id.name: archetype_id
archetype_id.documentation: The archetype of the item's root, when it is archetyped.

template_id.name: template_id
template_id.documentation: The template the item was committed under.

paths.name: paths
paths.documentation: The parts of the item the access reached, as fully qualified runtime paths, where it reached less than the whole item; empty when the whole item was reached.

categories.name: categories
categories.documentation: The categories of data the item belongs to, coded in a terminology the jurisdiction names.

origins.name: origins
origins.documentation: The systems the item's data came from.

was_delivered.name: was_delivered
was_delivered.documentation: True when the item was delivered to the accessor or written; false when it was asked for and withheld.

invariants.Item_named: object /= Void or version_id /= Void or not categories.is_empty

ACCESS_ORIGIN.name: ACCESS_ORIGIN
ACCESS_ORIGIN.documentation: One origin of accessed data: the system it came from, as `FEEDER_AUDIT` or the version's own `AUDIT_DETAILS._system_id_` names it, or the endpoint a federated access asked.

endpoint.name: endpoint
endpoint.documentation: The endpoint the access asked, for a federated access.

location.name: location
location.documentation: The facility at the origin, as `FEEDER_AUDIT_DETAILS._location_` names it.

ACCESS_QUERY.name: ACCESS_QUERY
ACCESS_QUERY.documentation: The query of an access by query. The query text is recorded as a digest by default; the text itself only where a policy asks for it.

stored_query.name: stored_query
stored_query.documentation: The qualified name of the stored query executed, with its version.

language.name: language
language.documentation: The query language and its version, such as `AQL 1.1`.

text_digest.name: text_digest
text_digest.documentation: Digest of the query text as received, in lower-case hexadecimal, with the algorithm of the log's chain.

text.name: text
text.documentation: The query text as received, recorded only where a policy asks for it.

rows.name: rows
rows.documentation: The number of result rows the query delivered that hold data of this entry's EHR.

ACCESS_AUTHORISATION.name: ACCESS_AUTHORISATION
ACCESS_AUTHORISATION.documentation: One ground the access decision rested on.

kind.name: kind
kind.documentation: The kind of ground, coded in the openEHR Terminology `access authorisation` group: a role, a treatment relationship, an agreement, a consent decision, a permit, an emergency override, the subject's own access, a representation, or a legal obligation.

policy.name: policy
policy.documentation: The policy or agreement the ground is defined in.

name.name: name
name.documentation: The name of the agreement or policy.

version.name: version
version.documentation: The version of the agreement or policy.

reference.name: reference
reference.documentation: The identifier of the decision the ground rests on, such as a consent decision reference or a data permit number.

legal_grounds.name: legal_grounds
legal_grounds.documentation: The legal provisions the ground rests on.

ACCESS_CHANNEL.name: ACCESS_CHANNEL
ACCESS_CHANNEL.documentation: The interface and request that carried an access.

interface.name: interface
interface.documentation: The interface, such as openEHR ITS-REST 1.1.0, HL7 FHIR R4 or a user interface of the system, coded in a terminology the system names.

request_id.name: request_id
request_id.documentation: The identifier of the request in the recording system's own logs; every entry one request produced carries the same value.

correlation_id.name: correlation_id
correlation_id.documentation: The identifier the client or an intermediary correlates the request by in its own log.

client_address.name: client_address
client_address.documentation: The network address the request came from.

ACCESS_RETENTION.name: ACCESS_RETENTION
ACCESS_RETENTION.documentation: How long an entry is kept, set when it is written from the categories and origins of the data and the laws that apply.

retain_until.name: retain_until
retain_until.documentation: The last day the entry is kept; Void when it is kept without end.

grounds.name: grounds
grounds.documentation: The provisions that set the period, such as a minimum period from the date of access and a national maximum.
